evidence.title: Kostantiniyye / Istanbul Imperial Metropolis (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ottoman imperial tahrir surveys & 1885 Ottoman municipal census
evidence.summary: Ottoman imperial capital rebuilt around the Süleymaniye kulliye, Topkapi workshops, Mediterranean naval yards, and late imperial ministries into the 1885 census.
evidence.limits: Earlier totals draw on household tax surveys and provisioning records across intra-mural, Galata, and Üsküdar districts.

population.note: 1885 Ottoman municipal census of Istanbul urban districts

evidence.title: Safavid Isfahan & Naqsh-e Jahan Imperial Square (1598–1736 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Safavid royal chronicles & New Julfa Armenian merchant records
evidence.summary: Shah Abbas I transformed Isfahan into the Safavid silk capital uniting the royal bazaar, Masjid-e Shah, and resettled New Julfa Armenian merchant quarter across the Zayandeh River.
evidence.limits: Metropolitan numbers contract steeply after the 1722 siege and subsequent Afghan-Afshar wars.

population.note: Mid-17th-century Safavid capital and New Julfa peak estimate (Chandler/Modelski)

evidence.title: Hangzhou & Jiangnan Grand Canal Terminus (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ming–Qing prefectural gazetteers & Grand Canal tribute ledgers
evidence.summary: Southern terminus of the Grand Canal linking Jiangnan silk workshops, woodblock printing houses, and Qiantang salt revenues into late imperial China’s coastal economy.
evidence.limits: Urban population was disrupted sharply during the 1860s Taiping conflicts prior to late-century recovery.

population.note: Late Ming Jiangnan commercial and silk metropolis estimate
High Qing Hangzhou prefectural urban estimate

evidence.title: Kyoto Imperial & Nishijin Silk-Weaving Metropolis (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Tokugawa machi household registers & Meiji prefectural counts
evidence.summary: Imperial court seat rebuilt under Nobunaga, Hideyoshi, and the Tokugawa bakufu as Japan’s center for fine silk weaving, lacquer, tea culture, and publishing.
evidence.limits: Demographic peak preceded the 1869 Meiji court move to Tokyo.

population.note: Early Tokugawa Kyoto urban register and court estimate
Late Tokugawa Kyoto commoner and craft quarter estimate

evidence.title: Osaka (Naniwa): Tokugawa Rice Exchange & Merchant Port (1583–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Dōjima rice exchange records & Osaka machi census rolls
evidence.summary: Shogunal commercial hub ("Kitchen of the Realm") linking Kitamaebune coastal grain ships, warehouse domains, Dojima futures trading, and Osaka textile mills.
evidence.limits: Castle-town garrison precincts were enumerated separately from chōnin merchant wards.

population.note: Mid-18th-century Tokugawa Osaka commercial ward peak estimate
Meiji Osaka industrial municipal census expansion (1898 register)

evidence.title: Honolulu (Kou Harbor) & Hawaiian Kingdom Capital (1809–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Missionary & Hawaiian Kingdom constitutional censuses (1831–1896) and 1900 Census
evidence.summary: Natural deep-water reef harbor developed into Kamehameha I’s royal residence, printing seat, diplomatic port, and capital of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi through 1900.
evidence.limits: Early 19th-century estimates reflect severe introduced epidemic losses documented across island censuses.

population.note: First missionary-Kingdom census estimate for Honolulu urban settlement (1831–1832)
1890 Hawaiian Kingdom official census for Honolulu town (22,907)

evidence.title: Warrane / Sydney & Port Jackson Colonial Port (1788–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: NSW 1828 Muster/Census & Australian colonial decennial censuses to 1891
evidence.summary: Eora (Gadigal) coastal country where the 1788 penal landing grew into New South Wales’s administrative capital, wool-export port, and rail-suburban city.
evidence.limits: Early colonial counts excluded dispersed Aboriginal nations across Sydney Basin and hinterland districts.

population.note: 1828 New South Wales first full colonial census for Sydney Town (~10,815 enumerated)
1851 NSW census for Sydney municipality and inner suburbs
1891 New South Wales colonial census for Greater Sydney (~383,283)

evidence.title: Gondar Imperial Capital & Fasil Ghebbi (Ethiopia, 1636–1855 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Solomonic royal chronicles & basalt castle stone-mortar fabric
evidence.summary: Permanent Solomonic capital founded by Emperor Fasilides north of Lake Tana, integrating multi-towered palaces, churches, illuminated scriptoria, and trade guilds.
evidence.limits: Royal authority decentralized during the Zemene Mesafint era after 1769 prior to Téwodros II.

evidence.title: Harar Jugol Walled Emirate & Islamic Scholarship Hub (1520–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Adal–Harari chronicles, five fortified gates & mosque inscriptions
evidence.summary: Sixteenth-century walled commercial city linking Ethiopian highland coffee, ivory, and Red Sea Zeyla caravans through 82 mosques and distinctive courtyard dwellings.
evidence.limits: Archaeological stratigraphy in densely inhabited core remains mostly conserved beneath standing neighborhoods.

evidence.title: Adwa Highland Basin & Solomonic–Modern Ethiopian Frontier (1880–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ethiopian royal state archives & treaty historiography (Treaty of Wuchale / 1896 Adwa)
evidence.summary: Highland trade junction in Tigray where Menelik II’s mobilized national army defeated Italian colonial forces in March 1896, securing Ethiopian sovereignty across the 1900 horizon.
evidence.limits: Represents documented state sovereignty campaign and caravan crossroads rather than single-building excavations.

evidence.title: Lamu Old Town (Kenya): Omani–Swahili Coral-Stone Port (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Patriarchal stone-house dendrochronology, poetry manuscripts & coral-rag masonry
evidence.summary: Unbroken coral-rag limestone Swahili port and Kiswahili literary center maintaining dhow monsoon commerce between East Africa, Hadhramaut, and western India.
evidence.limits: Continuous occupation limits deep trench exposures beneath historic street grid.

evidence.title: Zanzibar Stone Town & Busaidi Indian Ocean Sultanate (1698–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Omani Sultanate customs ledgers, coral mansions & treaty records
evidence.summary: Commercial capital moved by Seyyid Said from Muscat in 1840, structuring clove plantation exports, Indian banyan finance, ivory caravans, and later abolition treaties.
evidence.limits: Maritime entrepôt prosperity relied heavily on coerced caravan and plantation labor until late-19th-century abolition.

evidence.title: Mbanza Kongo Imperial Capital & Kulumbimbi (Angola, 1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Kongo royal correspondence, cathedral masonry & archaeological survey
evidence.summary: Highland capital of the Kingdom of Kongo under Afonso I and successors, uniting provincial taxation, rafia cloth exchange, literate Christian royal bureaucracy, and diplomacy.
evidence.limits: Portuguese-Kongo wars and mid-17th-century civil conflict fragmented royal centralization after 1665.

evidence.title: Mengo & Kasubi: Buganda Lacustrine State Architecture (1700–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Royal barkcloth-and-reed architecture & Lake Victoria canoe fleet records
evidence.summary: Northwestern Lake Victoria kingdom centralized around Kabaka courts, reed-thatched royal tombs (Muzibu-Azaala-Mpanga), iron-barkcloth tribute roads, and naval fleets.
evidence.limits: Organic timber-and-reed architecture requires periodic traditional rethatching and reconstruction.

evidence.title: Ambohimanga & Merina Unification of Highland Madagascar (1787–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Merina oral-historiographic corpus, stone gates & terraced rice engineering
evidence.summary: Sacred hill capital from which Andrianampoinimerina and Radama I unified the central Malagasy plateau through Betsimitatatra wet-rice irrigation and stone fortifications.
evidence.limits: Peripheral coastal sakalava and southern polities retained varied autonomy across the 19th century.

evidence.title: Kumasi & the Asante Confederacy Golden Stool State (1701–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Asante court goldweight metallurgy, adobe shrine relief & Great Roads network
evidence.summary: Forest state confederated by Osei Tutu and Okomfo Anokye from 1701, controlling Brong-Akyem goldfields, northern kola caravans, and stamped courtyard shrines around Kumasi.
evidence.limits: Royal palace structures at Kumasi were burned during Anglo-Asante wars in 1874 and 1896, leaving outlier shrines at Ejisu-Besease.

evidence.title: Old Oyo (Oyo-Ile) Cavalry Empire & Savanna–Forest Corridor (1600–1836 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Earthwork wall surveys, terracotta-paved palace courtyards & radiocarbon dates
evidence.summary: Tsetse-margin Yoruba cavalry power projecting authority from the savanna across Oyo-Ile earthworks toward Egbado and Atlantic coastal ports.
evidence.limits: Northern internal conflicts and Fulani jihad raids forced abandonment of Old Oyo south to New Oyo around 1836.

evidence.title: Abomey Royal Palaces & Kingdom of Dahomey (1625–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Polychrome bas-relief palace walls, earthen fosses & royal regalia archives
evidence.summary: Centralized Fon monarchy governing plateau agriculture, female Mino palace corps, Whydah coastal customs, and 19th-century palm-oil diplomacy from walled compounds.
evidence.limits: Later 19th-century walls reflect French conquest fires of 1892 and twentieth-century museum conservation.

evidence.title: Benin City (Edo) Earthworks & Early Modern Brass Guilds (1501–1897 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Iya moats, Igun Eronmwon lost-wax brass corpus & European factory accounts
evidence.summary: Oba court metropolis ringed by monumental earthen Iya ramparts, producing royal commemorative brass plaques and hosting regulated pepper, ivory, and cloth trade to 1897.
evidence.limits: Chronology of specific cast plaques depends partly on stylistic cross-correlation after 1897 dispersal.

evidence.title: Kanem–Bornu Capitals: Birni Ngazargamu & Kukawa (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Fired-brick palace ruins west of Lake Chad & Diwan/Girgam chronicles
evidence.summary: Saifawa empire under Idris Alooma using Ottoman firearms, cavalry highways, and brick capitals across the Komadugu Yobe basin to control central Saharan salt-and-horse trade.
evidence.limits: Rabih az-Zubayr’s invasion in 1893 destroyed Kukawa shortly before colonial partition.

evidence.title: Sokoto Caliphate & Kano Dyed-Indigo Cloth Walls (1804–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Fulani Arabic scholarship archives, Kano mud-wall circuit & indigo dye-pits
evidence.summary: Confederated Hausaland Islamic state led by Usman dan Fodio uniting Kano textile artisans, trans-Saharan leatherworkers, and savanna agricultural estates across 19th-century northern Nigeria.
evidence.limits: Urban wall circumferences span multiple medieval-through-19th-century rebuilding phases.

evidence.title: Elmina (São Jorge da Mina) & Gold Coast Stone Forts (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Portuguese, Dutch WIC & British customs forts along Fante-Akan coast
evidence.summary: String of coastal stone trade castles documenting shifting Akan gold exports, Atlantic slave-trade forts, Fante brokers, and Dutch/British coastal rivalry.
evidence.limits: Architectural fabric emphasizes European-garrisoned castles more than inland African town quarters.

evidence.title: Gorée Island & Senegambia Atlantic Crossroads (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Signare coral-limestone townhouses, naval charts & trade records
evidence.summary: Volcanic island anchorage off Cape Verde serving as a fortified Atlantic waypoint for gum arabic, hides, French West African commerce, and the Middle Passage memory.
evidence.limits: Archaeological deposits combine European military masonry with African domestic precincts.

evidence.title: Table Bay / Cape Town (//Hui !Gaeb): Khoekhoe–VOC Port (1652–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: VOC Dagregister, Robben Island stone quarries & Cape archival censuses
evidence.summary: Dutch East India Company refreshment station planted in Goringhaicona and Peninsular Khoekhoe grazing territory, linking enslaved Asian/East African craftspeople, wine farms, and British Atlantic commerce.
evidence.limits: Frontier dispossession progressed rapidly northward and eastward beyond Cape Peninsula surveys.

evidence.title: KwaZulu State: Bulawayo, uMgungundlovu & Ulundi (1816–1887 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated amakhanda cattle-byre rings, ironworking slag & Natal archives
evidence.summary: Centralized Nguni kingdom forged under Shaka through age-regiment amakhanda capitals, short-spear tactics, cattle-exchange hierarchy, and 1879 Anglo-Zulu resistance.
evidence.limits: Thatch-and-wattle kraal settlements preserve principally floor clay, ash pits, and stone foundations.

evidence.title: Cairo Citadel, Bulaq Press & Nile Delta Modernizing Hub (1517–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ottoman court registers, Bulaq printing press & 19th-c. canal engineering
evidence.summary: Imperial provincial metropolis connecting Arabian Sea Mocha coffee guilds, Waqf Madrasa endowment complexes, 1820s industrial cotton canals, and early Arabic printing.
evidence.limits: Distinct from medieval Fusṭāṭ layers represented in foundational Nile urban series.

evidence.title: Tunis Medina, Hafsid–Ottoman Corsairs & Husainid Beylik (1534–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Zaytuna mosque waqfs, Husainid palaces & Mediterranean consulate treaties
evidence.summary: Autonomous Ottoman regency and Husainid Beylik weaving olive oil, fez-cap workshops, Sahara-Sahel leather imports, and 1857/1861 constitutional reforms around historic Medina souks.
evidence.limits: Eighteenth-century rural tribal taxation varied significantly outside Sahel coastal plains.

evidence.title: Algiers Kasbah & Ottoman Mediterranean Regency (1516–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Barbarossa-era naval harbor bastions, Dey palaces & urban citadel terraces
evidence.summary: Stepped whitewashed hillside citadel guarding central Maghrebi maritime trade, Andalusian artisanal quarters, and corsair naval treaties prior to 1830 French conquest.
evidence.limits: Coastal bombardment and nineteenth-century colonial boulevard cuts reshaped the lower marine district.

evidence.title: Meknes Imperial City of Sultan Moulay Ismail (1672–1727 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Alawid monumental rammed-earth Heri es-Souani granaries & Bab Mansour gate
evidence.summary: Massive imperial palace city of rammed earth and green-glazed ceramic tile built as the Alawid state hub organizing Morocco’s central army and Saharan caravan tributes.
evidence.limits: Many imperial pavilions suffered severe damage during the 1755 Lisbon earthquake.

evidence.title: Marrakesh: Saadian Badi Palace, Sugar & Timbuktu Expedition (1554–1800 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Saadian marble tombs, Sus sugar-mill ruins & 1591 trans-Saharan chronicles
evidence.summary: Saadian capital powered by Sus valley cane sugar exports to Europe and Ahmad al-Mansur’s 1591 Songhai campaign establishing trans-Saharan salt-and-gold links.
evidence.limits: Monumental Badi Palace marble was partly dismantled in the late 17th century under Alawid patronage.

evidence.title: Chinguetti, Ouadane & Oualata Desert Manuscript Oasis Libraries (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Stone desert-town libraries containing thousands of early modern Arabic manuscripts
evidence.summary: Saharan stone caravanserai towns preserving family manuscript collections of astronomy, Maliki jurisprudence, medicine, and salt-caravan contracts across four centuries.
evidence.limits: Windblown sand encroachment obscures abandoned outer neighborhoods around ancient well fields.

evidence.title: At-Turaif in ad-Diriyah: Najdi Oasis Town & First Saudi State (1744–1818 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Mud-brick Najdi citadel architecture along Wadi Hanifa & Ottoman chronicles
evidence.summary: Walled adobe capital above Wadi Hanifa palm groves rising from 1744 into a peninsula-wide confederation before Ibrahim Pasha’s 1818 siege.
evidence.limits: Adobe superstructures suffered heavily in the 1818 bombardment and nineteenth-century abandonment.

evidence.title: Yaruba–Busaidi Oman: Nizwa, Bahla & Indian Ocean Maritime Empire (1650–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Aflaj hydraulic charters, Yaruba circular bastions & Muscat treaty archives
evidence.summary: Combined aflaj gravity-canal oasis agriculture in interior Oman with ocean-going baghlah fleets projecting Omani rule from Muscat to Mombasa and Zanzibar after 1650.
evidence.limits: Interior Imamate towns and coastal Sultanate capitals operated in shifting political balance.

evidence.title: Kashan Fin Garden & Qajar Hydraulic Oasis Estates (1590–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Qanat spring inscriptions, Safavid pool geometry & Qajar pavilion frescoes
evidence.summary: Iranian desert garden watered continuously by Sulaymaniyah qanat springs through Safavid velvet-weaving prosperity and nineteenth-century Qajar constitutional crises.
evidence.limits: Site represents elite hydraulic estate planning rather than provincial agrarian demography.

evidence.title: Baku Caspian Entrepôt, Shirvanshah Palace & Caravan Networks (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Limestone Inner City caravanserais, Shirvan stone relief & silk custom records
evidence.summary: Fortified Caspian Sea harbor exchanging Shirvan raw silk, naphtha oil, and Iranian cotton between Safavid, Ottoman, and Astrakhan Volga merchants before 19th-century oil boom.
evidence.limits: Seventeenth- and nineteenth-century fortifications overlay medieval walled layouts.

evidence.title: Bukhara, Khiva & Kokand Shaybanid–Manghit Oasis Khanates (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Shaybanid madrasa tilework, Bukhara Jewish & Indian merchant deeds & waqf rolls
evidence.summary: Caravan-guild city-states sustaining overland Astrakhan–Kashgar horse, tea, and silk exchanges long after Cape sea routes opened.
evidence.limits: Chronicles often concentrate on Bukhara and Samarkand mosques over pastoral steppe hinterlands.

evidence.title: Agra & Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi): High Mughal Architecture & Revenue Empire (1556–1857 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ain-i-Akbari revenue cadastres, marble pietradura & Yamuna riverfront plans
evidence.summary: Agra and Shah Jahan’s planned Yamuna capital integrated zabt land-revenue surveys, monsoon water-chutes, Persian-Sanskrit translations, and global silver rupee minting.
evidence.limits: Imperial treasury and palace grandeur coexisted with sharp regional famine vulnerabilities in 1630–1632 and 1783.

evidence.title: Lahore Walled City, Shalimar Gardens & Sikh Confederacy Capital (1584–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Imperial Akbar–Shah Jahan brickwork, Ranjit Singh court archives & urban plan
evidence.summary: Punjab crossroads serving successively as Akbar’s northern court, Ranjit Singh’s centralized Khalsa empire capital (1799–1849), and nineteenth-century canal-colony administrative center.
evidence.limits: Eighteenth-century conflicts damaged several outer Ravi gardens prior to Sikh restorations.

evidence.title: Old Goa (Velha Goa) & Maritime Indian Ocean Crossroads (1510–1843 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Mandovi estuary cartaz port registers & Basilic masonry complexes
evidence.summary: Arabian Sea entrepôt connecting Malabar pepper, Konkani shipyards, Jesuit printing presses, and Deccan horse imports prior to seventeenth-century Dutch blockades and Panjim shift.
evidence.limits: Ecclesiastical ruins dominate above poorly preserved artisanal suburbs.

evidence.title: Amber & Planned City of Sawai Jaipur / Jantar Mantar (1592–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Sawāi Jai Singh Sanskrit–Arabic zij tables, 1727 urban grid & masonry instruments
evidence.summary: Kachwaha Rajput fortress and 1727 gridded pink-sandstone capital hosting the monumental stone Jantar Mantar astronomical observatory synthesizing Sanskrit, Arabic, and European star tables.
evidence.limits: Grid design covers walled royal wards rather than surrounding Aravalli villages.

evidence.title: Pune & Sahyadri Maratha Hill–Sea Fort Network (1646–1818 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Chhatrapati Shivaji coronation records, Peshwa Modi script daftar & Sindhudurg
evidence.summary: Western Ghats mountain and island forts linking Maratha cavalry logistics and Angre naval defense from Raigad and Pune across much of eighteenth-century South Asia.
evidence.limits: Peshwa paper archives reflect literate Brahmin chancelleries more completely than rural peasant holdings.

evidence.title: Murshidabad–Dhaka–Calcutta Muslin Textiles & Colonial Transition (1576–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Bengal Subah cotton customs ledgers, VOC/EIC factory rolls & decennial censuses
evidence.summary: Hooghly–Ganges–Brahmaputra delta corridor shifting from Dhaka fine muslin looms and Murshidabad banking houses into an industrialized nineteenth-century colonial port metropolis.
evidence.limits: Delta urbanization numbers fluctuate between river-port relocation and nineteenth-century census consolidation.

evidence.title: Lhasa: Potala Palace, Jokhang & Ganden Phodrang (1642–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Fifth Dalai Lama monastic chronicles, Red Palace murals & plateau treaties
evidence.summary: Tibetan political-monastic complex elevated by the Fifth Dalai Lama in 1642, coordinating monastery tax estates, woodblock Tibetan canon printing, and Qing frontier ambans.
evidence.limits: High-altitude rural nomad herds remained sparsely recorded in monastic town listings.

evidence.title: Macau & Canton Thirteen-Factory Silver–Porcelain Exchange (1557–1842 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ming–Qing Hoppo customs customs rolls, Japanese Iwami/Potosí silver records
evidence.summary: Pearl River estuary hinge funnelling New World and Japanese silver ingots into Jingdezhen porcelain, Zhejiang silk, and Fujian tea before the Opium War treaty system.
evidence.limits: Customs figures record official licensed cargoes while undercounting coastal junk smuggling.

evidence.title: Suzhou Gardens, Cotton Looms & Jiangnan Silver Economy (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ming–Qing lineage land deeds, cotton merchant guild stelae & canal maps
evidence.summary: Canalled Jiangnan manufacturing capital whose specialized silk, cotton, and printing markets integrated single-whip silver taxation and scholar-literati garden estates.
evidence.limits: Urban gardens reflect elite gentry patronage rather than tenant-weaver households.

evidence.title: Fujian Tulou & Southern Maritime Diaspora Communities (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Genealogical zupu books, rammed-earth timber ring beams & lineage charters
evidence.summary: Monumental multi-story rammed-earth circular clan dwellings across southwestern Fujian valleys integrating tea terraces, lineage defense, and Hokkien/Hakka maritime networks.
evidence.limits: Individual tulou beam dates span sixteenth-century foundation through twentieth-century repairs.

evidence.title: Chengde Mountain Resort & Multi-Ethnic Qing Steppe Diplomacy (1703–1860 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Manchu–Mongol–Tibetan stone stelae, Putuo Zongcheng temples & court archives
evidence.summary: Kangxi and Qianlong summer capital north of the Great Wall built with Tibetan and Mongol lamaist temple architecture to host Khalkha, Zunghar, and Torghut audiences.
evidence.limits: Site fell into royal disuse following mid-19th-century geopolitical crises.

evidence.title: Shuri Castle & Maritime Kingdom of Ryukyu (1501–1879 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Rekidai Hōan diplomatic archives, Naha port stone causeways & Ryukyu lacquer
evidence.summary: Okinawan maritime kingdom balancing tributary embassies to Beijing, commerce across Siam and Java, and post-1609 Satsuma subordination until Meiji 1879 annexation.
evidence.limits: Original Shuri wooden halls were largely destroyed in 1945 and reconstructed over stone foundations.

evidence.title: Nagasaki–Dejima & Edo-Period Global Botanical/Scientific Exchange (1641–1859 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: VOC Nagasaki factory Daghregister journals & Japanese Rangaku translations
evidence.summary: Artificial fan-shaped harbor islet regulating Edo Japan’s Dutch and Qing merchant enclaves, silver/copper exports, medical anatomy texts, and astronomical instrument imports.
evidence.limits: Dejima represented a tightly policed trade window alongside separate Tsushima–Korea and Satsuma–Ryukyu corridors.

evidence.title: Himeji-jo & Tokugawa Castle-Town Urbanization (1601–1871 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Plaster-walled tenshu joinery, sankin-kōtai stipends & domainal castle surveys
evidence.summary: Flagship white-plaster multi-keep castle anchoring the Tokugawa daimyo road-and-market urban system under sankin-kōtai alternate attendance.
evidence.limits: Defense architecture highlights samurai-domain mobilization rather than rural farm villages.

evidence.title: Nikkō Tōshō-gū & Tokugawa State Ritual Network (1617–1868 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Cedar-avenue pilgrimage roads, lacquer-gold carvings & shogunal itineraries
evidence.summary: Mausoleum complex enshrining Tokugawa Ieyasu as state protector, visited by Korean and Ryukyuan diplomatic processions along the cedar-lined Nikkō Kaidō.
evidence.limits: Reflects state ritual authority and artisanal guilds under the Tokugawa pax.

evidence.title: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress & Late Joseon Silhak Engineering (1794–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Hwaseong Seongyeok Uigwe construction blueprint manual & granite bastions
evidence.summary: King Jeongjo’s 1794–1796 walled administrative city south of Seoul combining Korean stone walls with Jeong Yak-yong pulley-cranes and wage-paid artisan labor.
evidence.limits: Original late-18th-century documentation survives in exceptional detail via Uigwe manuals.

evidence.title: Hué Imperial Citadel & Nguyễn Dynasty Vietnam (1802–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Châu Bản Nguyễn imperial vermilion records & Perfume River citadel walls
evidence.summary: Capital unified by Emperor Gia Long in 1802 across northern and southern Vietnam, linking Confucian state exams, Vauban-influenced moat walls, and royal tombs.
evidence.limits: Late-19th-century French protectorate treaties sharply reduced imperial autonomy outside ritual administration.

evidence.title: Ayutthaya Cosmopolitan Siam Trade Entrepôt (1501–1767 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Chao Phraya brick prangs, foreign quarter excavations & Royal Chronicles
evidence.summary: Island river metropolis integrating Siamese royal monasteries, Persian/Chinese/Japanese/Portuguese merchant villages, deer-hide and sappanwood exports until the 1767 sack.
evidence.limits: High water table and modern urbanization limit full preservation of wooden residential suburbs.

population.note: Early modern Siamese capital including Chao Phraya foreign quarters (Chandler/Reid estimates)

evidence.title: Luang Prabang & Lan Xang Upper Mekong Buddhist Court (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Wat Xieng Thong mosaic stupas & Mekong riverine monastery charters
evidence.summary: Confluence Buddhist seat founded earlier as Xiang Dong Xiang Thong that anchored eighteenth-century Lao royal patronage and upland-river forest-product trade.
evidence.limits: Political partitioning of Lan Xang after 1707 divided Luang Prabang, Vientiane, and Champasak courts.

evidence.title: Melaka, Aceh & Straits Monsoon Crossroads (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Malacca Malay–Portuguese–Dutch–Peranakan strata & Straits custom books
evidence.summary: Strategic narrow-straits port transitioning from Malay Sultanate law codes through Portuguese and Dutch VOC fortresses to multi-ethnic Peranakan Baba–Nyonya and British Straits Settlements.
evidence.limits: Early sultanate wooden waterfront remains mostly buried beneath reclaimed fort layers.

evidence.title: Vigan & Ilocos–Manila Maritime Chinese–Philippine Town (1572–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Bahay na bato coral-lime mansions, kiln pottery & Iloko–Mestizo guilds
evidence.summary: Northern Luzon coastal trading grid merging Ilocano carpenters, Fujian Sangley merchants, and Pacific galleon networks in seismic lime-plaster townhouses.
evidence.limits: Urban grid highlights merchant family blocks rather than upland Igorot gold-trading trails.

evidence.title: Mataram–Yogyakarta Court City & Javanese Batik/Agrarian Culture (1586–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Javanese babad chronicles, Kraton water-castles & VOC-era agrarian registers
evidence.summary: Central Javanese kraton political order emerging from Sultan Agung’s Mataram through the 1755 Giyanti partition into royal Yogyakarta and Surakarta court centers.
evidence.limits: Central Javanese focus leaves northern Pasisir port Sultanates such as Banten and Makassar partially underrepresented here.

evidence.title: Saadian–Alawid Fez Craft Guilds & Copper-Leather Quarter (1550–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Guild hisba regulations & Fez el-Jdid cannon works
evidence.summary: Moroccan artisanal and theological hub sustaining brassworking, Chaouara leather tanneries, and Andalusian-descended scholarly lineages into late-19th-century reforms.
evidence.limits: Supplemented by separate Fes Medina urban chronology.

evidence.title: Murzuq & Ottoman Fezzan Caravan Sultanate (1551–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Awlad Muhammad dynasty fortresses & Tripoli Saharan caravan diaries
evidence.summary: Oasis transit capital in southwestern Libya linking Tripoli Mediterranean ports directly with Bornu around Lake Chad across the central Sahara.
evidence.limits: Surface mudbrick remains reflect frequent late Ottoman restorations.

evidence.title: Ségou & the Bamana Middle Niger Cavalry State (1712–1861 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Coulibaly & Diarra royal oral epics, tondjon fortresses & mud-mosque towns
evidence.summary: Non-Islamic Bamana state centered along the Middle Niger organized around age-set warrior cohorts (tondjon), riverboat fisheries, and cotton-strip currency prior to El Hadj Umar Tall’s 1861 conquest.
evidence.limits: Oral epic chronologies cross-checked against nineteenth-century traveler journals.

evidence.title: Djenné Inland Delta Mosques & Fulani/Toucouleur Caliphates (1501–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Sudano-Sahelian masons guild architecture & Hamdallahi chronicles
evidence.summary: Niger Inland Delta market town linking Dogon plateau ironwork, Masina pastoralists, Songhai river fleets, and nineteenth-century Hamdallahi islamic reform.
evidence.limits: Periodic seasonal floodplains reshape mud structures every decade.

evidence.title: Nsheng (Kuba Kingdom) Wood Carving & Raffia Cloth Federation (1625–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Shyaam royal oral genealogy (solar eclipse anchor) & Kasai court collections
evidence.summary: Sankuru–Kasai central African forest-savanna kingdom unified around Shyaam a-Mbul a-Ngoong, famous for New World maize/cassava adoption, cut-pile Kasai velvet raffia, and royal ndop sculptures.
evidence.limits: Early colonial rubber extraction and border violence severely disrupted Kuba villages around 1900.

evidence.title: Lunda–Mwata Yamvo Copper & Salt State in Katanga–Kasai (1600–1890 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Mwant Yav court titles, copper croisette ingots & Angola caravan accounts
evidence.summary: Savanna woodland empire organizing tributary lukano bracelet investiture from eastern Angola toward Lake Tanganyika, exporting Katanga copper crosses and ivory.
evidence.limits: Chronology blends genealogy with documented Atlantic and coastal exchange dates.

evidence.title: Delagoa Bay & Gaza Nguni Trade Networks (Mozambique, 1545–1895 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Inhambane–Sofala customs archives & Gaza Manhlagazi capital records
evidence.summary: Southeastern African coastal bay exchanging inland Shona gold, hippopotamus ivory, and cattle for Indian glass beads before Soshangane’s 1820s Gaza state consolidation.
evidence.limits: Focuses on major bay and court nodes rather than scattered upland homesteads.

evidence.title: Bakhchisarai Khan’s Palace & Pontic Steppe Trade (1532–1783 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Crimean Khanate diplomatic defters, Ottoman stone port Kefe & Khan Saray
evidence.summary: Tatar-Ottoman steppe court bridging Nogai steppe pastures, Black Sea maritime custom houses, and Eastern European diplomacy until 1783 Russian annexation.
evidence.limits: Nineteenth-century imperial rebuilds altered several courtyard annexes.

evidence.title: Ottoman Aleppo Khans & Levantine Overland Silk Exchange (1516–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Shar’iyya court inventories, Khan al-Gumruk architecture & Levant merchant accounts
evidence.summary: Northern Syrian stone bazaar metropolis linking Persian raw silk caravans, Iraqi soap/spice routes, and Iskenderun Mediterranean galleys.
evidence.limits: Declined proportionally after 17th-century Persian wars and 1869 Suez Canal opening.

evidence.title: Mamluk–Ottoman Baghdad & Basra Shatt al-Arab Maritime Trade (1534–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Ottoman Pashalik salname yearbooks, Basra date-trade & Gulf shipping lists
evidence.summary: Twin Tigris–Euphrates commercial hubs exporting Iraqi dates and Arabian horses down the Persian Gulf while receiving Indian cotton textiles.
evidence.limits: Severe plague outbreaks (e.g. 1831) caused sharp short-term population contractions.

evidence.title: Surat Mughal Port & Gujarati Maritime Banking Guilds (1573–1850 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Mughal Bandar-i Mubarak port customs books & European factory diaries
evidence.summary: Premier Mughal Arabian Sea port connecting Gujarati indigo and calico weavers, Bohra/Parsi shipwrights, hundi credit bills, and Red Sea Hajj fleets prior to Bombay’s rise.
evidence.limits: Siltation of the Tapti estuary shifted oceanic traffic southward during the 18th century.

evidence.title: Coromandel Calico Coast: Masulipatnam, Madras & Pondicherry (1600–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Chintz mordant-dyed textile guilds & EIC/Compagnie des Indes port ledgers
evidence.summary: Southeastern Indian textile littoral exporting mordant-painted cottons to Southeast Asia, West Africa, and Europe throughout the 17th–18th centuries.
evidence.limits: Deindustrialization pressures during the 19th century transformed weaving districts significantly.

evidence.title: Golconda Fort & Hyderabad Qutb Shahi–Asaf Jahi State (1518–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Charminar masonry, Deccan diamond mine chronicles & Nizam court records
evidence.summary: Deccan plateau kingdom linking Krishna Valley alluvial diamond fields, Telugu/Dakhni poetry, Persianate architecture, and Masulipatnam export corridors.
evidence.limits: Focused on urban Charminar–Golconda corridor rather than interior Gond and Telangana agrarian belts.

evidence.title: Johor–Riau Sultanate & 1819 Singapore Free Port Nexus (1528–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Sejarah Melayu court recensions & Straits Settlements decennial trade censuses
evidence.summary: Successor Malay–Bugis Riau-Johor maritime polity later joined by 1819 free-port transshipment bridging Chinese gambier/pepper planters, Bugis prahus, and South Asian merchants.
evidence.limits: Urban port records capture maritime commerce more fully than Orang Laut sea-nomad settlements.

evidence.title: Manila Intramuros–Parián & Acapulco Silver Galleon Hinge (1571–1815 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Almojarifazgo port registers & Parián Chinese artisan market excavations
evidence.summary: First continuous trans-Pacific trade terminus exchanging Mexican-Andean silver pesos directly for Zhangzhou Fujian silk, ivory carving, and Southeast Asian spices.
evidence.limits: Official galleon manifests record crown cargoes while omitting private coastal junk exchanges.

evidence.title: Kingdom of Kandy (Sri Lanka): Highland Sanctuary & Cinnamon Frontiers (1505–1815 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Temple of the Tooth timber-pillared halls & Kandyan diplomatic conventions
evidence.summary: Mountainous Sinhala Buddhist kingdom holding the central Sri Lankan highlands against three centuries of Portuguese, Dutch, and early British expeditions until 1815.
evidence.limits: Monastic charters detail land tenure across wet-zone valleys better than northern dry-zone villages.

evidence.title: Kiakhta & Maimaicheng Sino-Russian Tea & Fur Caravan Border (1727–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: 1727 Treaty of Kiakhta customs diaries & Shanxi merchant caravan account books
evidence.summary: Twin Russian-Qing border depot north of Lake Baikal/Selenga funneling Shanxi brick tea, Chinese cotton textiles, and Siberian squirrel/sable pelts overland for 150 years.
evidence.limits: Customs ledgers capture official caravan trade prior to Trans-Siberian railway rerouting.

evidence.title: Kashgar, Yarkand & Altishahr Oasis Guilds under Qing Rule (1759–1900 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Khoja-era waqf deeds, Beg administrative registers & Tarim jade-tea custom posts
evidence.summary: Tarim Basin oasis towns governed through local Uyghur Beg officials under Qing frontier garrison administration, mediating Fergana cotton, Khotan nephrite jade, and Tibetan tea commerce.
evidence.limits: Oases were periodically shaken by 19th-century Khoja rebellions and Yaqub Beg’s Emirate (1865–1877).
